# V1 Handoff Findings Ledger

Open defects, gaps and blockers found while landing the all-WIP consolidation
(PR 116) for the 2026-10-05 move to a new development machine. Each finding
records its observed evidence and explicit acceptance obligations. Order work by
the release dependencies below and register current ownership through
`docs/ops/MULTI_AGENT_COORDINATION.md`; finding numbers are stable identities,
not execution priority. When a repair lands, retain its stable ID, dated evidence and exact qualification scope in the
fixed history, with remaining family obligations linked to their existing open
owners. Do not delete findings or discard earlier failure or measurement evidence
when status changes.

Cite a commit of the same landing as `change:I` plus 8 to 40 hex digits of
its `Change-Id` trailer; `tools/molt_dev.py integrate` rewrites the citation
to the landed commit id ([integration contract](../ops/INTEGRATION.md)). Cite a
landed commit by its commit id.

Evidence paths under `C:\Molt\...` exist only on the Windows host that
produced them; the public CI run IDs are enough to reproduce each finding.

From 2026-10-06 the primary development host is macOS (Apple Silicon). The
Windows host stays available for platform testing. Host paths are in
`docs/agent/ORCHESTRATION.md` (Canonical paths).

## Release decision and exit scope

**V1.0 release is held.** This ledger is the authoritative open-findings and
exit-status index. Passing local checks or implementing a producer does not
qualify a release. The machine-checked requirements remain owned by
[the public contract](../spec/PUBLIC_CONTRACT_V1.md),
[phase exit requirements](../../config/phase_exit_requirements.toml), and
[the release acceptance matrix](../../config/release_acceptance_matrix.toml).
Every outstanding correctness, security, resource, performance, packaging and
portability finding below is part of the V1.0 exit scope. No finding may be
accepted as debt, waived or deferred past release qualification. Close a finding only
after its complete consumer family is integrated and its stated acceptance
evidence passes; retain its stable ID, integrated repair and explicit unverified
coordinates. Consolidation must preserve every requirement and machine-consumed ID.

The [Python contract](../spec/areas/compat/contracts/verified_subset_contract.md)
bounds excessive dynamism that obstructs efficient compilation and standalone
execution. It does not shrink to the currently passing tests. CPython source and
applicable official PEPs govern admitted semantics; missing support, incorrect
behavior, performance defects and unverified cells remain release obligations.
Verification records evidence for that scope. Its development-side checks do
not add unnecessary work to emitted binaries.

Tools read this ledger only through `tools/finding_status.py`. A row in a
section whose title starts with "Fixed" is closed, and every other finding row
is open. An exact "(was X)" renames finding X; any other parenthetical names a
part and closes nothing. A fixed row records its fix or verification evidence in
its last cell. `tools/release_exit_gate.py` reads this file at the release source
commit. It refuses PASS to a version that claims the v1 public stable contract
(major 1 or later) while any row is open; a v0.x bundle records and reports the
open rows. The H0 phase exit lists each open row as an open obligation.

This closure standard applies retrospectively to every earlier finding,
including the historical fixed rows below. A landed repair does not establish
closure of its bug family. Closure requires a failure-mechanism search through
sibling implementations, producers and consumers; one corrected authority;
independent regression controls that exercise the actual boundary; and explicit
coverage of affected target and platform cells. Recurring integration or proof
failures must be traced to their shared cause as well. Reconcile uncovered
instances and missing qualification into the existing owning open requirement;
retain the historical repair evidence without treating it as release acceptance.

### Development cost and release discipline

The runtime's shared path-join builder replaces repeated accumulated-prefix copies
with linear accumulation and removes the duplicated join intrinsics. A retained
paired macOS arm64 lexical-core measurement at 16,384 24-byte components records
32,770 to 17 allocation/reallocation requests and 10,065,911,841 to 950,255
cumulative requested bytes. Median local latency is 69,604.12 to 58.14 microseconds.
The measurement harness runs only during development. These are lexical-core
measurements, not peak memory, whole-program speedup or Windows qualification. The native path, pathlib, linecache and byte-glob
consumers pass their affected native comparisons. At `6cbbfeff8`, WASM path
and pathlib pass while byte-glob fails; remaining platform cells retain their
explicit acceptance obligations.

Source-local bounded compiler batches and symbolic module/code ownership remove
cross-program recompilation without adding a guest registry or per-call lookup.
The measured two-program second build fell from 59.868s to 13.658s (one
development-profile comparison); V1-07 retains the full scope and remaining
acceptance. Development checks, cache retention and proof custody stay on the
development side.

Automatic cache retention now reuses the existing guarded controller after
payload closure. The separate maintenance queue job, supervisor provisioning,
database coalescing and timeout are deleted. The canonical prune lock owns
cross-process throttling, and the same selected environment owns protected
paths. Forty-three focused checks pass, including real closed-payload execution
and an ordinary cleanup error preserving the payload result. The registered
run at `852e428ac` scans 1,417 entries in 13 ms under the same guard, launches
no maintenance queue job and preserves the primary compilation failure. That
build exposed one missing class-cleanup export reference; `19b4a05e9` corrects
it before runtime qualification. This repair
adds no work to emitted programs; broader build-footprint obligations remain
with V1-07/HF-10.

Superseded closed development runs now enter the existing run-retention window
instead of remaining pinned merely because their shared Cargo target exists.
The existing target lease and immutable terminal receipts establish a distinct
closed successor; current, busy, failed, pinned and ambiguous runs stay
protected. Retention removes only the old run's logs and scratch, preserving
Cargo outputs and custody CAS. All 32 focused ownership, race and recovery
controls pass; the unchanged-source control reproduces the old exemption.
The configured byte bound still covers eligible runs, not total disk usage.

Successful compiler-cache reuse now refreshes the existing eviction owner at
most once per five-minute maintenance interval. Shared archives, constituent
objects, frontend JSON, optional native sidecars and WASM bundles use their
existing admission and locks; stale eviction inventories are rechecked before
removal. Immutable entry contents and required outputs remain unchanged.
Focused controls distinguish hot-entry preservation from the old policy;
source review retains approximate recency and explicit protected-file boundaries.
At `6cbbfeff8`, all 17 Linux aarch64 Rust publication/admission controls pass,
including constituent round-trip, corruption rejection and prior-generation
preservation. Actual recency-specific queued reuse, other platform controls and
end-to-end build savings remain unqualified. This is compiler/development work
with no emitted-program cost.

Discovery and full frontend analysis now share the existing readonly AST
record when source, path, diagnostic filename and target match. Mutating
serial lowering parses its own tree, matching parallel lowering. Seventy
focused controls pass; unchanged-source and incomplete-migration controls
detect the redundant parse and shared-tree mutation. Five-sample host analysis
medians fall from 47.1 to 14.8 ms for asyncio and from 42.0 to 15.4 ms for
asyncio.tasks, with identical analysis facts. These are isolated analysis
measurements; whole-compile latency and target execution remain unmeasured.

Archived failed Cargo generations can now be reclaimed through the existing
queue lifecycle after authenticated physical closure and full archive
verification. Three actual Linux reclamations recover 3,434,692,608 bytes in
13.96 seconds; their original failed proof status is preserved. Unclosed or
leased generations remain protected. This development-only path adds no
emitted-program work; other filesystem/platform cells remain unqualified.

on Linux aarch64 measure 20,000 exact-integer-key operations per workload with
128 prewarmed entries. Median bounded hits fall from 174.32 to 58.34 ns/op,
unlimited hits from 165.97 to 21.68 ns/op, bounded churn from 3,469.71 to
3,298.67 ns/op, and unlimited growth from 3,383.52 to 3,274.30 ns/op. Each
workload improves in every pair. The miss after the bounded hit streak falls
from 751.86 to 5.06 microseconds as stale recency records fall from 20,128 to
128. A separate allocation pair records 20,000 to zero temporary managed
allocations per loop; these counters exclude Rust metadata allocations.

The tradeoff is explicit: bounded-churn recency capacity's logical payload
proxy grows from a median 6,880 to 11,872 bytes, while the hit-streak proxy
falls from 527,872 to 7,168 bytes and unlimited recency storage becomes zero.
These proxies are not physical allocator measurements. The retained images,
raw samples and independent interpretation qualify this coordinate only;
collision-heavy keys, other capacities, targets and product-level performance
acceptance remain unverified.

Existing build diagnostics now retain phase files for affected differential
consumers. A Linux aarch64 changed-runtime native build takes 55.206 seconds:
36.826 seconds in Cargo runtime construction, 41.773 seconds in backend
preparation overall, and 2.136 seconds in application backend compilation.
These nested intervals must not be added together. A later reconciled I/O
batch takes 110.2 seconds for its changed compiler/runtime build and 11.1
seconds for the next consumer with unchanged Rust inputs. These are bounded
development observations, not matched speedups. Reuse the existing phase
reporter, freeze complete runtime families before rebuilding, and distinguish
changed-artifact construction from unchanged-input compiler overhead. No
instrumentation enters emitted programs.

before opaque compound commands execute. Four actual shell-consumer controls
cover every Cargo wrapper selector, preserved endpoints, disabled incremental
compilation and durable temporary directories; all 17 gate-environment controls
pass. The policy remains development-side. Thirteen mandatory WASM test
sites now execute their actual guarded Node program directly, removing a
duplicate version-probe process and an ineffective optional-tool selector at
each site. Their 41 affected Rust controls pass; genuinely optional tool cells
keep their existing admission policy.

the oracle requires it. Ten affected controls pass, including real completed

The existing reference, determinism and performance authorities remain the
release path: pinned CPython source and observations; perturbation of irrelevant
compiler inputs; reference-output agreement before timing; and the positive

owners without creating another framework. Native/WASM matrix qualification,
installed execution without Python, security/resource repairs and positive
performance admission remain open in the dependency buckets below.

## Release dependency and landing order

Land complete changed authorities as soon as their actual consumers pass. Keep
one integration candidate, reconcile retained donor work against its current
base, and delete each replaced internal path in that same migration. A broader
open release finding does not require holding an independently complete repair;
an unmigrated consumer does. Reuse unchanged accepted inputs rather than
restarting unrelated proofs after every edit.

| Work bucket | Next complete outcome and owning findings | Verification that changes the decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Integration | Finish and land the existing runtime/ABI candidate and its consumer migration; reconcile remaining SOURCE/cache/writer donors against current main (V1-01/V1-09/V1-12/V1-25/V1-28). Delete replaced lanes with their consumers. | Reuse retained runtime/ABI results; execute the still-unqualified affected public native/WASM consumers and required lint once. Recheck only inputs invalidated by a repair. Source identity, failure atomicity and complete migration determine landing readiness. |
| Correctness and conformance | Close shared compiler/runtime, frame/exception/async, C-ABI and container protocols; versioned tokens/Unicode/errno, codecs, JSON, imports and compression follow their existing authorities (V1-05/V1-14–V1-18/V1-21–V1-23/V1-26–V1-30, HF-02/HF-95/HF-104/HF-106). | One independent CPython-source or kernel/API counterexample per changed invariant, then the affected semantic family. Retain minimized seeds and exact outputs. Defer the complete target/version/profile campaign until a coherent candidate is stable; do not replace missing semantics with narrower claims. |
| Security and resources | Complete TLS/socket and descriptor boundaries, VFS file identity, real process synchronization, physical resource charging and bounded retention (V1-10/V1-11/V1-13/V1-19/V1-20/V1-33/V1-34). Address concrete safety failures before dependent performance work. | Actual boundary tests for ownership, coercion, extent, callback/reentry, denial and cleanup on the affected platforms. Unit success cannot establish missing native/WASM behavior; unrelated broad suites add no evidence for these boundaries. |
| Installed delivery | Make installed compile/edit/run, LLVM and required runtime delivery, package/extension custody and native/WASM scientific witnesses complete (V1-01/V1-02/V1-06/V1-24/V1-28, HF-04). | A complete installed success path and independent failure controls, using the exact delivered artifacts. Emitted programs execute where host/fallback Python is unavailable; installed users need no Cargo build of Molt. Reproduce current extension seals before E1. |
| Performance | Complete the positive measured-metric producer/receiver path early, then remove measured bottlenecks in algorithms, runtime, startup, artifact size, memory and compilation (V1-07/V1-19–V1-21/V1-27/V1-29/V1-30, HF-26/HF-79/HF-132). | One representative authenticated measurement path first; matched before/after metrics for each load-bearing change. Measure scaling where complexity changes. Run the required performance matrix once the candidate and metric contract are stable; a microbenchmark cannot replace product acceptance. |
| Release and developer experience | Close lossless output, effective differential/property/fuzz coverage, maintainable dependencies, bounded CI/build cost and reproducible authenticated publication (V1-03/V1-04/V1-06/V1-08/V1-12/V1-25 and the open CI/harness findings). | Test the actual changed automation boundary. Reuse valid evidence and existing commands; avoid another framework or full-suite fanout. Final current-candidate E1–E4 and authenticated H0 cover the declared matrix and all open obligations before v1.0 publication. |

These are work buckets, not six serial phases or separate backlogs. Complete the
current integration outcome first; keep disjoint safety/correctness repairs and
the installed/performance acceptance paths moving as capacity permits. Findings
retain their single owning rows even when a shared invariant crosses buckets.
The dependencies do not require one giant patch or universal new capabilities
beyond the declared support contract.

Verification has a decision boundary. Before dispatch, name the changed
invariant, the defect an independent oracle would detect, and the result needed
to proceed. Use the smallest existing proof that resolves that uncertainty.
After it passes, run an actual affected-consumer group only when migration,
platform behavior or product execution remains unproved. Preserve exact input
identities and reuse unaffected passing evidence. Do not repeat runtime/ABI
suites for documentation, isolated tooling or unchanged semantic inputs; do not
add tests for trivial reversible edits or implementation mirrors. Broad
conformance, performance, supply-chain and release matrices are candidate
qualification work, not a per-edit ritual. A new failure justifies widening to
its affected family, not restarting every green lane.

Development checks must earn their cost by exposing a concrete defect or
establishing a required acceptance claim. Do not add a new required gate merely
because a checker exists. Retire duplicated checks and obsolete fixtures as the
canonical boundary takes ownership; retain independent oracles and the final
release obligations. Every existing open finding remains an exit obligation.
Compiler startup/build/link
cost, emitted-guest execution/memory cost, development verification cost and
release supply-chain cost must be measured and attributed separately. Proof
capture and release signing stay on the development/release side; installed
users and emitted guests pay only for their required product behavior.

Machine-checked authorities remain `config/phase_exit_requirements.toml`,
`tools/phase_exit_manifest.py`, `tools/release_exit_gate.py`,
`tools/public_contract_gate.py` and the linked acceptance matrix above.

## Engineering and acceptance rules

Every change must distinguish development/compiler work from execution in the
shipped end-user binary. Source custody, proof instrumentation and release
evidence belong on the development side. Additional runtime work must implement
a concrete runtime requirement and justify its measured cost; do not charge
development validation to guest startup, allocations or execution.
Eager work requires a concrete correctness requirement or reproducible evidence
that it improves the relevant workload. Otherwise defer it to its first real
consumer, preserve failure atomicity, and avoid duplicate ownership or caches.

CPython source at the declared reference version is the semantic source of
truth. Source-grounded implementation and version-matched independent execution
must agree before a Python semantic finding can close; a fixture or local test
result alone cannot redefine the contract.

## Open: correctness and release blockers

| ID | Finding | Evidence | Next step |

| HF-441 | A compiled native program keeps the `SIGPIPE` and `SIGXFSZ` dispositions it inherited, so a write to a pipe whose reader closed ends the process with `SIGPIPE`, and a write past the file size limit ends it with `SIGXFSZ`. CPython ignores both at startup, so the write fails with `EPIPE` and raises `BrokenPipeError`, or fails with `EFBIG` and raises `OSError`. Both native code owners agree (AOT executable and JIT runner); only `molt-runtime/src/async_rt/process/native_io.rs` ignores `SIGPIPE`, and only once the program spawns a process. | Twin probes, macOS arm64, 2026-10-21 (HF-371 review): `os.write` to a pipe with a closed reader exits -13 under AOT and JIT; CPython 3.12.15 prints `BrokenPipeError` and exits 0. `prog \| head -1` exits -13 under AOT and JIT; CPython raises `BrokenPipeError` on the next write, reports `Exception ignored in: <_io.TextIOWrapper name='<stdout>' ...>` when it flushes stdout at exit, and exits 120. `tests/differential/basic/closed_pipe_write_signal.py` pins the native behavior as an expected failure in the twin gate. `SIGXFSZ` (HF-371 review v5, 2026-10-22, macOS arm64): a program that writes 10 bytes under `ulimit -f 0` prints `start` and exits -25 under AOT and JIT; CPython 3.12 prints `start` and `OSError 27` and exits 0. `tests/differential/basic/file_size_limit_write_signal.py` pins it. | Do what CPython does (`signal_install_handlers` in `Modules/signalmodule.c`): ignore `SIGPIPE` and `SIGXFSZ` once in runtime start-up (`molt_runtime_init`, both code owners), raise `BrokenPipeError` from `EPIPE` and `OSError` from `EFBIG` on every write path, flush stdout at exit with CPython's exit status 120 and "Exception ignored" report on a broken pipe, and restore the default disposition in spawned children as `subprocess` does (`restore_signals=True`). Then turn `closed_pipe_write_signal.py` and `file_size_limit_write_signal.py` into passing cases on native and JIT, add a `\| head -1` case, and check WASM, which has no signals. |
| HF-442 | Native recursion has no stack guard. A program that raises the recursion limit and recurses deeper than the native stack ends with `SIGSEGV`; CPython 3.12 raises `RecursionError` at the limit. Each compiled Python call uses native stack, and nothing checks the remaining stack before the guard page is hit. | Twin probes, macOS arm64, 2026-10-21 (HF-371 review): `sys.setrecursionlimit(1_000_000)` with unbounded recursion exits -11 under AOT and JIT with empty stderr, after printing `start`; CPython 3.12.15 raises `RecursionError` at the limit (0.5 s). Before the review fix the JIT runner aborted with Rust's "has overflowed its stack" message (-6). `tests/differential/basic/native_stack_exhaustion.py` pins the native behavior as an expected failure in the twin gate. | Do what CPython 3.12 does: count native recursion depth and raise `RecursionError` before the stack runs out. CPython 3.12 counts C recursion depth (`Py_C_RECURSION_LIMIT`) separately from Python frames, and Rust puts guard pages on its threads; HotSpot and V8 compare the stack pointer with a per-thread limit at function entry. Give compiled code a stack-limit check at the entry of functions that can recurse, with the limit taken from the thread's stack bounds and guard page, keep guard pages on every runtime thread, and raise `RecursionError` with CPython's message. Then turn `native_stack_exhaustion.py` into a passing case on native and JIT, and prove WASM, whose stack exhaustion traps. |
| HF-455 | A compiled native program does not start as CPython does when a standard descriptor is closed. With file descriptor 0 closed it crashes in bootstrap; with fd 2 closed it finds fd 2 open: the native runtime opens `/dev/null` read-only at start, and with fd 2 free that descriptor becomes fd 2. `os.fstat(2)` then succeeds, and `sys.stderr` writes go to a read-only `/dev/null` instead of failing as on a closed descriptor. CPython leaves a closed standard descriptor closed, sets `sys.stdin`, `sys.stdout` or `sys.stderr` to `None` (`create_stdio` checks `is_valid_fd`) and runs. | Twin case `tests/differential/basic/closed_stderr_start.py` (HF-371 review v3), macOS arm64, 2026-10-22, lane tip on main 80a5dc469: the program restarts itself through `/bin/sh -c 'exec "$@" 2>&-'`; CPython 3.12 prints `child ran, stderr closed`, and the AOT executable and the JIT image both print `child ran, stderr open` (exit 0). `lsof` of an AOT program started with `2>&-` shows fd 2 and fd 4 as `/dev/null` opened read-only. Both tiers share the runtime, so the case is an expected failure (`closed_stderr_reused_by_runtime`) that pins the exact ending both must share. Closed stdin (HF-371 review v4, 2026-10-22, AOT executable and JIT image started with `<&-`): both exit 1 with `KeyError: 'maxsize'` in `_validate_bootstrap_scalars` (`src/molt/stdlib/sys.py:450`, from `_init_metadata_views` at line 478 during `sys` import in `builtins.py` line 25); CPython 3.12 runs. Closed stdout runs under all three. | Owner: runtime startup (`runtime/molt-runtime` initialization and the native launch). Find the call that opens `/dev/null` at start (`fs_usage` or `dtruss` on macOS, `strace -f -e openat` on Linux on the AOT program above), and open every descriptor the runtime holds for itself close-on-exec and above fd 2 (`F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC` with a minimum of 3), so a closed standard descriptor stays closed. Then do what CPython does: when fd 0, 1 or 2 is not valid at start, make `sys.stdin`, `sys.stdout` or `sys.stderr` `None`. For closed stdin, find why the bootstrap scalars lose `maxsize` (the startup read of fd 0 or a descriptor that lands on it) and add a twin case that starts a program with `<&-` and pins CPython's output. Remove the expected-failure mark from `closed_stderr_start.py`, so the twin case passes against CPython on native, JIT and WASM. |

Repaired: an explicit `--cpython-dir` is used verbatim (default `third_party/cpython-<version>`); `--cpython-custody shard-plan --shard-plan <plan>` makes the digest-bound shard plan the tree's custody (`_load_plan`, pinned `cpython_commit`, the plan's own directory) and `nightly_sharding` passes it for regrtest shards; preflight keeps the warmup budget until one build succeeds. Regrtest shards (Nightly 38663831687): the Molt shim is regrtest's worker, and it never enforced `--timeout`. CPython's own workers stop a test there through faulthandler; regrtest kills a worker only at min(1.5 x timeout, timeout + 300 s), and that kill does not reach the `molt` process tree. The run also kept no per-test record, so a killed shard reported every test unfinished. Repaired, awaiting a Nightly run: the shim stops each test at the timeout (`TIMEOUT`) and appends one row per test (`tools/compat/regrtest_results.py`); `cpython_regrtest.py --deadline-s` admits only tests whose timeout still fits (the rest report `DID_NOT_RUN`, reason `deadline`); the summary's item rows come from that log, and the shard runner recovers it after a kill, through the same `ItemOutcome` path as differential shards. Differential OOM retries now recheck the same run admission cutoff before each serial retry; a completed OOM keeps its original result when another full test no longer fits, and no retry is announced without admission. The owning host controls pass (633 tests, one skip), including an actual guarded sleeping child: one typed item budget is pinned before dispatch, uses the same target-specific phase policy as admission, and includes CPython, interpreter/LLVM preflight, batch startup/strict retries and native dyld/daemon/cache recovery. Workers and retries cannot renew it. Suite preflight uses the absolute suite deadline; warm-cache work reserves its build-only phase. Expiry refuses new work while preserving original timeout/resource/infrastructure results; exhaustion during backend evaluation retains the selected backend rows. Batch completion performs no redundant interpreter probe. Suite evidence reads only the execution context’s explicitly selected marker, through the shared reader; ambient artifact locations cannot override it. Parallel worker diagnostics publish once at completion to the chosen detail sink or console; the supervisor retains statuses and timings rather than completed output payloads, including across OOM retry. Case-log names use the shared repository-relative identity and a fixed-size digest, avoiding path escapes, separator collisions and filename limits. Nightly and real process-pool/platform qualification remain open. Mandatory cleanup, synchronous filesystem calls and summary publication retain outer-guard headroom; this is not a hard wall-clock bound on arbitrary OS operations. |

| HF-463 | Molt's two Lima VMs (`molt-linux`, `molt-x86`) were made by hand, and no tool defined or checked them. Apple's virtiofs server keeps one host file open for each inode a guest has looked up, until the guest forgets it, so the guests pinned host files the host deleted: on 2026-10-22 `molt-linux` held 802 files under ~/Molt and 167 deleted files; on 2026-10-17 `molt-x86` held 188 files of worktrees in the Trash until it stopped. `molt-linux` mounted the whole home, not `~/Molt`, and Lima forwarded every guest port to the host: 13 (`molt-linux`) and 832 (`molt-x86`) since their boot on 2026-10-21 (the HF-F251 class). | (1e91e9f23, 6598fd7cb): `tools/linux_vm.toml` defines both VMs: resources, image, Rosetta, containerd, the guest clone, and the declared port forwards, after which the renderer appends a rule that ignores every other guest port. It mounts no host path, so a guest pins nothing by construction; `tools/linux_vm.py push` sends a commit into the guest clone over Lima's SSH (30 commits 0.19-0.20 s, against 0.27-0.36 s for the guest to read them through the mount; a 181 MB tree 0.56-0.61 s against 0.61-0.65 s). `check` compares `limactl list --json` with each definition field by field and exits 1 on drift: any mount, or a `lima.yaml` newer than its hostagent. Mechanism, measured 2026-10-22 on Linux 7.0 (`molt-linux`) and 6.8 (`molt-x86`): `echo 2 > drop_caches` makes the guest forget every unused inode (its inode count returns to baseline; the hiprio queue completes each forget), but the server closes forgotten descriptors only at every 64th `FUSE_FORGET`, so up to 63 stay open with no time limit. `echo 1`, `echo 2`, `echo 3`, a lookup sweep of the deleted paths and `vfs_cache_pressure` 10000 each freed nothing. So HF-463's first release (one drop) freed nothing in the review's 7 drops, its "45 of 47 freed" did not reproduce, and the two Git objects it kept were waiting in the server's batch, not in use in the guest. For a VM that still mounts host paths, `release` now runs a drop, a lookup of 64 forget-set files under each mount and a drop: on both kernels it freed every deleted file the guest had read, stat'ed, listed or mapped, and kept a file a guest process held open until that process exited. Lane retirement releases a VM only when it holds files under the retiring paths or deleted files, and never stops the cleanup on a failure. It spawns nothing when every live VM runs its definition (0.4-0.9 ms); otherwise it costs 85-90 ms for an unmounted path, 213 ms for a mounted one with nothing held and 565-622 ms with a release of both VMs (host load 7-9). `apply` keeps the first replaced config as `lima.yaml.molt-previous` and never overwrites it, restores and restarts the replaced config when the VM fails to start, and refuses a busy guest: a guest-user or login-session process outside the idle set, a subordinate-id process, a containerd shim, a package install; it does not see root work outside a login session (runbook). Design, mechanism evidence and options: `docs/design/linux_vm_apparatus.md`. Tests: `tests/tools/test_linux_vm.py` (fake `limactl` and `lsof` and a fake server that closes per 64 forgets, so a drop-only release fails; Lima's validator on the rendering; real Git for `push`; the opt-in `MOLT_LINUX_VM_TESTS=1` test against the real guests passed on both) and the retirement tests in `tests/test_molt_dev.py`; 15 mutations each fail a test. End state, 2026-10-22: `apply` installed both definitions and kept each first replaced config as `lima.yaml.molt-previous` (`molt-linux` had mounted `~`, `molt-x86` `~/Molt`); its start killed both hostagents (HF-471), and the operator restarted both with `limactl start`. Since then `tools/linux_vm.py check` exits 0 (0.22-0.65 s) and no guest mounts a host directory (`findmnt -t virtiofs`: none in `molt-linux`; in `molt-x86` only Apple's Rosetta share, `/mnt/lima-rosetta`). Lima 2.2.1 did not rewrite `lima.yaml` at start (both files predate their hostagents' `ha.pid`), so `runs_its_definition` holds for both and retirement spawns nothing (1.31 ms). Not run: a real `push` (it writes guest state; neither guest clone has a pushed ref yet). |

A pytest argv that is not an exact plan row is a focused proof. | HF-219 | Backend daemons never exited: no idle timeout or owner-lifetime bound, so every distinct socket kept a daemon until reboot (29 idle daemons held 3.4 GB on 2026-10-17). The launcher and the `molt_diff` pruner also killed any daemon whose socket was gone unless a Python-side `retiring` mark said otherwise, so a daemon that retired by itself would have lost the compile it was draining. | The daemon owns its lifetime. It retires after `MOLT_BACKEND_DAEMON_IDLE_TIMEOUT` seconds (default 1800) with no live connection, and the clock starts when the last connection ends, so a long compile never shortens it (sccache's arrival-based timer would). Retirement unlinks only the socket the daemon bound (device and inode), so a successor on the same path keeps its own, and logs why it retired. The launcher never stops a socketless daemon and drops an exited daemon's record without a warning; the `molt_diff` pruner requests graceful retirement only from a verified idle responder over its RSS budget, and never sends speculative age/silence kills; the identity record's `retiring` mirror is deleted. `integrate --cleanup-worktree` retires the checkout's daemons before it removes the worktree. Sizing: 7 request gaps reconstructed from daemon logs (86% under 5 min, the rest 1.5-2.3 h breaks) give the same hit rate for any timeout from 5 min to 1.5 h, and an idle daemon held about 117 MB; the sample is small, so the default is a measured range, not a fitted value. Verified on macOS arm64: molt-backend bin tests (126 passed, including idle retirement, a live connection holding the daemon, the idle clock and a successor's socket) and the `daemon_server` tests that spawn the real binary; 96 launcher and pruner tests and the cleanup tests; each new oracle bite-checked against the old behavior. The follow-up ownership hardening also preserves poll deadlines across EINTR, rounds positive fractional milliseconds up, checks observed process birth before a maintenance request, and avoids process/identity scans when RSS maintenance is disabled. Its 24 Python pruning controls and 573-test consolidated compiler/IR graph passed on macOS arm64. Linux is unverified; the daemon does not run on Windows. |

Lookup, both publication tiers, LRU and flights share it; request strings move and equal tiers share one handle. Actual native/WASM producer-to-replay controls cover both tiers and every target option, with changed-target misses leaving absent IR leases unopened. The 45-test owning daemon aperture passed on macOS arm64; the native-only graph also owns disabled-WASM parsing. No wire-schema adapter, serialized target list or guest check. | HF-F142 (was HF-137) | The Python child broker resolved a Windows launch through the child's PATH, PATHEXT and cwd. CPython's `Popen` passes `executable` as lpApplicationName and the `list2cmdline` string as lpCommandLine (`Lib/subprocess.py`, 3.12), and `CreateProcessW` resolves the image in the calling process: its image directory, its current directory (unless `NeedCurrentDirectoryForExePathW` says no, which applies only to a name without a backslash), the system, 16-bit system and Windows directories, then the caller's PATH, appending only `.exe`. The child's `env` and `cwd` take no part, and a given `executable` is completed from the caller's current directory and never searched. So the broker could admit a child-PATH or child-cwd decoy, or a `.com` that PATHEXT ranks first, while Windows ran another image, and it refused launches Windows would run. The hook also split a Windows command line with `shlex`, not CreateProcess's rule. Microsoft's text says `.exe` is not appended to a name with a path, but its own example appends it; on hosted Windows Server 2022 it is appended to both `C:\...\tool` and `./tool`, so HF-137's `./cargo` runs `cargo.exe`. The Node hook shared the child-PATH rule; it launches the broker's selection, but libuv appends `.com` or `.exe` to a selected path without an extension and runs that file. The native supervisor hashes every created image (`CREATE_PROCESS_DEBUG_EVENT`), so a wrong admission was a hook error, not a closure escape under native supervision. | `tools/proof_queue_pkg/windows_createprocess.py` owns the CreateProcessW model; the broker picks the model from the hook's authenticated runtime and the host. On Windows the Python hook reports `executable`, the command line and the caller's facts: image (`GetModuleFileName`), current directory, PATH from the process environment block (`os.putenv` bypasses `os.environ`) and `NeedCurrentDirectoryForExePath`. Where the documentation conflicts or is silent (a path-qualified name without an extension, a relative name with a separator, empty, quoted or relative PATH entries, a directory hit), the broker admits only an image that every reading runs; device, drive-relative, stream, wildcard, traversal and trailing-dot names fail closed. POSIX keeps the child-PATH rule. A Node selection on Windows must have an extension. A table from the documentation checks the model on every host (37 cases). `test_python_hook_broker_admits_the_image_createprocess_runs` sends 15 launches through the same `Popen` call twice, plain and under the real hook and broker; each child is created suspended, and its kernel image (`QueryFullProcessImageNameW`) is the oracle; no child-PATH, child-cwd, PATHEXT or image-directory decoy is admitted. `test_node_selection_names_the_image_libuv_runs` shows libuv running the `.exe` beside an extensionless path. Both pass on hosted Windows in CI 38031471885 attempts 2 and 3 (jobs 114171437224 and 114174710194), with all 58 Windows rows of the custody file; the 65 POSIX rows pass on hosted Linux and macOS (attempt 1). The cell's other failures are not this change: four `test_dx_run_context.py` rows (red on the base run 38027215773), the HF-76 identity-probe census rows, two real-Cargo rows of `tests/test_cargo_quarantine_custody.py` (cold cache, HF-139) and one real queue execution ending rc 2, which moved from `test_proof_queue_exec_records_passed_run` (attempt 2) to `test_guarded_receipt_uses_row_repo_root_and_exact_outer_binary_identity` (attempt 3), the HF-76 receipt symptom. ## Preservation

Everything removed while consolidating onto `main` is recoverable from bundles on the Windows host only: `C:\Molt\drift-bundles\handoff-20261005-final.bundle` (all 88 refs before branch deletion) and `handoff-20261005-final-worktrees.bundle` (final snapshots of every removed worktree), plus `stash@{0}` in `C:\Molt\molt-src` (the shared checkout's Sep 30 - Oct 1 working state, superseded by `main`).

Consolidation on 2026-10-14 reduced the repository to `main`, one working lane (`lane/opkind`) and the then-active Codex lane (`codex/v1-wip-integration`). Every other branch and worktree is recoverable from bundles in `~/Molt/drift-bundles/` on the Mac: `consolidation-20261014.bundle` (48 heads: 41 branches, among them the 21 pre-rewrite June `recovery/*` and `worktree-agent-*` branches, plus seven `refs/archive/codex-<worktree>` commits that snapshot the complete working state of each idle Codex worktree below, untracked files included) and `retired-lanes-20261014.bundle` (`lane/train-17` and `lane/hf12-runtime-gate`, superseded or declined under HF-12). Restore with `git fetch <bundle> <ref>:<ref>`. The retired worktree directories and their build trees are in the Trash until the owner empties it. Codex's committed work landed through the takeover of `codex/queued-cargo-selection` (PR 119); the snapshots stay donor material: reconcile files when the owning row's work starts and never apply a snapshot wholesale. Triage against the takeover tip on 2026-10-09 counted, per worktree:

| Worktree | Area | Contained | Applies cleanly | Conflicts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `shared-hash-storage` | runtime dict/set storage (V1-27) | 122 | 13 | 51 |
| `ci-source-audit` | runtime and C-ABI fixtures | 22 | 14 | 19 |
| `v1-ffi-retirement` | proof supervisor, queue and guard tooling | 6 | 99 | 53 |
| `v1-resource-contract` | resource contract, CLI and CI wiring | 15 | 48 | 71 |
| `v1-main-landing` | guard and queue tooling, Windows process API | 19 | 41 | 17 |
| `hf03-upstream-reconciliation` | WASI SDK and CLI consumers (17 commits on `codex/v1-coherent-wasi-sdk` beyond the takeover, plus WIP) | 0 | 18 | 9 |

On 2026-10-16 the orphaned `codex/v1-wip-integration` lane (46 commits beyond main, 272 uncommitted paths) and its clean successor `codex/v1-wip-convergence` were retired. `~/Molt/drift-bundles/codex-v1-wip-integration-20261016/` holds `branch.bundle` (the branch), `worktree.patch` (tracked changes against c4bf4ac32), `untracked.tgz` and `status.txt`. Two read-only audits found every one of the 33 non-merge commits and the whole working tree on main, byte-identical or in a later form (mostly through 1afa7afe4, 7ebbbc42c and 046a53722); conflicting files hold only older forms main replaced. The lane's ledger alone carried open obligations main does not name; they are recorded here unverified on current code: BLAKE PBKDF recognition and exact XOF-operation errors; CPython 3.12 shared instance-dictionary keys and `BytesIO` logical-size/reset ownership; tar archive direction, retained-file and completion semantics; the parser-payload transport; external zip constructors, decompressor dictionaries and full gzip read/seek conformance; the `RawIOBase` `_handle` cost baseline; the fresh allocation-refusal control as a separate proof; the user-database provider and optional-import graph migration.

## Retained integration evidence

### Compiler and runtime integration history

Compiler-record work under HF-266 proceeds in dependency order: borrowed-record
ownership, canonical backend records and storage, then persisted digest reuse
and transport. Assembly now replaces changed function/operation paths and
retains unchanged identities through normalization. This is compiler work; it
adds no emitted-program work. The record format and digest migrations remain
open until their complete consumer families are qualified.

Module serialization now emits canonical initializer and code-owner symbols
without program-owned slot allocation; serial and worker lowering persist that
form. Assembly validates and retains the records directly, and cached parameter
declarations are admitted without a normalization pass. Standalone program
serialization retains its own entry and allocation contract. The owning controls
pass, and eight paired frontend cells retain the previous assembled values.
Serialization context now belongs to a function walk: one 19,073-operation probe
reduced context constructions to 201 while preserving output. Its timings were
noisy and establish no wall-clock gain. Executable function records now carry no publication, GPU-origin or app-binding
facts. One symbol-keyed sidecar follows both artifact scopes through worker,
serial, schema-9 cache and integration admission. Native publication consumes
its indexed boundary before rewrites; GPU and app consumers receive their own
facts explicitly. Strict executable tools project through the same authority.
Module admission stages only local additions and commits after complete
validation, preserving shared state on refusal. Sixteen paired frontend cells
retain executable values and exact metadata; original eager integration fails
two unchanged-state controls. The integrated migration now implements compact
schema-9 function records, one shared four-kind source store, admitted-use
recency and global byte/age retention. Strong-identity digest seeds travel
through serial/parallel admission and survive only unchanged backend bodies;
one backend transition owns analysis and artifact-setup reuse. Its consumer,
resource and installed-delivery qualification is in progress under HF-266;
implementation is not acceptance.

Cache-consumer fixtures carry the same required metadata map as production.
Source-generation controls first admit a warm entry before changing or removing
its source; malformed-value controls retain a valid envelope so a missing field
cannot masquerade as rejection of the intended defect.

The same storage owner now accepts opaque byte records, and all existing import
scan and intrinsic-fact consumers own their unchanged JSON encoding and admission.
SQLite rejects oversized or non-BLOB rows before Python materializes their
payload. One actual 8 MiB over-limit read reduced Python peak allocation from
8 MiB to 1.3 KiB; this is a bounded allocation result, not a build-time claim.
Expanded Windows cache consumers exposed unsupported no-follow timestamp calls
and an unreadable ambient LLVM search entry. Recency now pins the admitted
generation, with native Windows birth-time comparison instead of assuming
pathname and handle `ctime` expose the same clock. Automatic LLVM discovery
shares the existing executable-search authority and excludes unknown provenance;
explicit selections retain configuration errors. Source-byte and archive-custody
fixtures preserve their independent oracles across newline and platform rules.
These changes remain compiler/development work. The existing five-minute file
recency policy is unchanged; a private Darwin probe measured about 9 microseconds
added per cold file refresh and unchanged hot-hit cost. Source-row recency now
uses revision-fenced SQLite observations rather than file timestamps. Those
historical file measurements do not qualify its new row-maintenance costs.
Binary module records and persisted digest reuse are implemented in the current
candidate; full consumer, performance and delivery acceptance remains open.

Source-record connections now follow operation and admitted-observation
ownership instead of a permanent process-wide root map. In a bounded Darwin
arm64 diagnostic over 100 disposable roots, abandoned owners fell from 100 to
zero, descriptors from 300 retained to zero retained, and observed RSS growth
from 23.9 MB to 1.4 MB; this does not qualify whole-build or installed costs.
Fresh compiler/development pool contexts also prevent inherited parent heaps
and locks. The sibling audit, frontend, environment and differential consumers
share that policy, including stop-state and creating-parent custody.
These are development/compiler changes with no emitted-program checks.

Binary-image analysis and backend artifact setup now share that single digest
owner after final IR rewrites. Analysis schema v3 retains original function
order, source locations and headers while composing admitted body hashes; the
replaced whole-IR JSON key is removed from the analysis layer. Its independent
cost control fails on the original full-payload hashing path. Current bounded
controls exercise seeded reuse, ordered invalidation, content-equal replay,
header/analysis-authority invalidation and the actual pipeline's shared owner.
At `c0bb75420`, all 36 selected Linux aarch64 integration gates pass, including
3,422 joined Python consumer cases with nine explicit skips. Actual native and
linked-WASM source builds match the retained CPython 3.12.15 reference with
Python removed from their execution path; all five command guards close without
orphan cleanup. One warm profiled before/after pair measures analysis-cache
lookup at 52.2/5.37 ms. This attributes the removed full-body serialization,
not a general wall-clock improvement. Broader target, installed-delivery and
performance acceptance remains under HF-266 and V1-07; these observations do
not close those findings.

Backend transport and its staging family are integrated at `00ddf32f2`.
Protocol 2 admits typed probe/file states; Python and Rust consume one packaged
version fact. One-shot, daemon and factgraph requests use sorted MessagePack
file leases and the shared typed regular-file reader. The retired inline lane
and duplicate JSON file reader are removed; public JSON export remains a
separate contract. All 42 selected Linux aarch64 integration gates pass,
including 4,547 joined Python cases with 17 explicit skips. Actual one-shot and
uncached daemon native builds and linked WASM match the retained CPython 3.12.15
output with an empty executable search path and Python environment variables
removed. Factgraph also succeeds. All seven command guards close without
termination reports, and the daemon reports one cache miss, no hits and normal
protocol retirement. These source-build observations do not prove host Python
absence, installed delivery or the release matrix. Compiler encoding and staging
costs, Windows SDK refusal and remaining acceptance stay with HF-266, HF-10,
V1-02, V1-07 and V1-12 below; no emitted-program work is added.

The storage/digest consumer migration is integrated at `4173741a6`: all 38
selected Linux aarch64 integration gates pass, including 4,763 joined consumer
cases with 17 explicit skips. The unchanged production storage/codec bytes
also passed 201 Windows x64 cases with three POSIX-only skips. A six-build
Linux aarch64/CPython 3.12 development cohort executes native cold, unchanged,
comment and body edits plus linked WASM before/after the body edit. Every
