WASM linking accounts for 52.1 of 137.5 measured build-phase seconds. There is
no matched baseline or general speedup claim. These remaining costs belong to
HF-266/HF-357 and V1-07.

That cohort also exposed a terminal cleanup defect: five build guards attempted
tracked-orphan cleanup after successful compiler exits. Historical receipts do
not retain those helpers' executable identities. A separate kernel wait oracle
reproduces the compiler's missing join of its owned spawn resource tracker
before root exit. The fast-exit authority now performs CPython's tracker stop
after completed thread/atexit callbacks, preserving borrowed spawn descriptors
and avoiding a new helper import for commands without workers. The owning
controls pass on Darwin arm64, and a pure-standard-library mechanism probe
passes on CPython 3.12.15, 3.13.12, 3.14.3 and 3.15.0 there. Its measured terminal
join takes 5.4–7.1 ms in that bounded cohort. This does not qualify arbitrary
raw-fork custody, whole-version support or all platform cells. At `364a126e0`,
all 13 owning controls and actual native/linked-WASM consumers pass on Linux aarch64/CPython 3.12.15. Both products match CPython
with Python removed from their execution path; all five command guards reclaim
scratch and close with no termination reports or tracked-orphan cleanup. This
qualifies that compiler exit cell, not the broader V1-12/HF-334 custody and
performance obligations. Output parity and eventual guard cleanup alone do not
close those obligations.

The current compiler-cost work reuses the cross-project lowering-cache repair
(HF-327) and one shared fast-profile Cargo cohort for the native-callable ABI
family. The remaining import-graph work belongs to HF-285: a retained 32-module
probe requested 1,633 distinct semantic scan records, including owner scans
revisited under revised namespace premises. Its unchanged replay accepted every
record and wrote none. Read-only replays of those same keys took 86 ms in the
existing store, so the earlier 2.89-second read phase does not establish a
persistent SQLite bottleneck. Bounded ingestion batching improved a separate
cold-write experiment but did not improve warm reads or establish better writer
tails; it is not an integrated optimization. Reduce proven repeated semantic
work before introducing another cache or storage protocol. These costs are
development/compiler work and add nothing to emitted programs.

The admitted AST now owns one module-export fact per target version and
namespace premise; graph-owner/argument projections and star-import discovery
share it, and the replaced target-only memo is deleted. In one isolated cold
Darwin arm64 graph pair, export computations fell from 1,634 to 74 and their
phase from 2.684 seconds to 0.064 seconds. All 1,633 persisted scan records were
byte-identical. Full graph time moved from 24.739 to 23.807 seconds; this single
ordered pair establishes no general wall-clock speedup. All 207 owning Python
controls pass, including source-generation, target and namespace separation;
the uncached-body control fails the repeated-work oracle. Namespace syntax now shares that admitted source lifetime as well; existing
resolved host-source and binding consumers reuse the same projection without
repeating normalization. Broader premise-driven scanning remains open under HF-285.

A source-frozen ten-build native/WASM consumer cohort on Darwin arm64
(logical `dev`, physical `dev-fast`, with changed runtime inputs) spent 551.7
seconds in recorded build phases: WASM linking used 231.0 seconds (41.9%),
backend preparation 164.2 seconds (29.8%), and module graphs 7.3 seconds (1.3%).
The existing build-phase reporter owns this breakdown. It identifies where to
measure and remove the remaining compilation cost under V1-07; it establishes
neither a no-change rebuild result nor comparative performance acceptance.

The bytes-regex consumer migration in HF-322 is bounded by
[the regex authority](../design/foundation/37_regex-engine-frontier.md).
Owned patterns, incremental scanner state and correct buffer custody do not
qualify matching complexity or full language parity. The matcher now compiles
one typed program and executes explicit continuation/capture/assertion state;
the replaced recursive AST interpreter and depth-limit false-no-match path are
deleted. Fullmatch and scanner advancement constrain acceptance, lastindex
records group closing order, and VM workspace allocation refusal propagates as MemoryError.
Fixed-width repeats retain bounded VM workspace, and literal assembly no longer
copies the growing prefix. General backtracking/restart complexity, versioned
Unicode and atomic/possessive semantics remain security, correctness and
performance exit obligations under HF-329. The design records implementation
separately from unqualified release capabilities. Regex semantic carriers now
share the canonical `re_parity.py` executable instead of paying for 27 separate
native/WASM program builds. The consolidation preserves all prior scenario inputs,
200 assertions and 447 CPython stdout lines; the owning storage/codec programs
remain separate. This reduces the owning cohort from 58 to six product builds.
At `61d642b2c`, all three owning programs pass native and WASM differential
execution on Linux aarch64, CPython 3.12.15, logical `dev` / physical `dev-fast`,
full stdlib. The regex program retains 677 CPython output records, including
atomic/possessive commit, raw surrogate identity, nested capture rollback, verbose
lexical admission and forward/reverse string iteration. All 34 selected integration
gates pass, including owning runtime allocation-failure controls. This qualifies
that development cell;
other versions/platforms/profiles, full parser diagnostics, complexity, signals,
Unicode and complete OOM behavior remain open under HF-329.

The shared text-storage migration removes regex's same-layer dependency on the
stdlib text crate and the foreign WTF-8 view that cannot represent adjacent
Python surrogate code points under its own invariant. Runtime core owns one
borrowed, allocation-free surrogatepass iterator and encoder for all consumers,
including generated charmaps and Windows paths. The crate-graph ratchet and the
pinned CPython boundary-byte oracle pass. Actual Linux aarch64 target-3.12
Unicode, bytes-regex and expanded codec consumers pass on native and WASM.
The bounded development-side kernel experiment rejected a slower
stack-buffer encoder. This source correction neither closes HF-329 nor proves
comparative runtime performance, full conformance or release acceptance.

Strided string slices now seek once through the existing UTF-8 index and move
one cursor across selected source spans instead of repeatedly decoding from
the beginning. This removes the quadratic decode pattern. Scalar indexing
still probes the ASCII prefix and uses the existing bounded cache; its
worst-case cost remains linear, not constant. HF-185 retains that indexing
cost and the required native/WASM comparative qualification.

Native build-identity acceptance requires all concurrent same-named programs
to compile successfully and execute their own code. Complete diagnostics and
native guard receipts attribute the intermittent failure to missing suite
custody under parallel pytest: a completed build's guard terminates its shared
compiler daemon while peers still use it. Even a passing nine-build replay
records six premature daemon terminations. The correction reuses one existing
controller-owned lease, inherited before workers start and closed after they
join. Serial sentinels and parallel sessions share the same scope authority;
parallel sessions add no RSS scanner. The existing native regression retains
structured errors, checks both program exit statuses and rejects command-owned
orphan termination. Corrected Linux aarch64 Python 3.12 qualification passes
all nine actual native builds and CPython output comparisons with zero
command-owned daemon kills and one suite transfer. The actual nested-worker
inheritance and terminal-close control passes on macOS. Broader platform,
shutdown and release-matrix obligations remain under V1-01 and V1-12.
Daemon diagnostic intervals can contain concurrent peers; they are not
request-exclusive evidence. Tail and interval reads now share the existing
byte-bounded reader and freeze the observed end before reading, removing a
whole-file tail read and open-ended append capture. Independent append and
byte-count controls detect both old defects. This bounded development-only correction is separate from the daemon
lifetime repair.

Tool availability must not silently select an unrelated command's ABI. Generic
CI and DX SDK setup publish availability and the C ABI receipt; runtime plans
and SDK proof commands explicitly select their Rust target. Local and CI
execution retain each command's declared tools across deduplication, pytest
batching and upstream binding, then project from the pre-admission caller
environment. One aggregate prerequisite check still reports all missing
capabilities before execution; repeated selections reuse their projection.
Independent actual-child controls detect the old SDK link-setting leak into
pure Rust consumers while retaining explicit user flags. Managed-runtime
startup remains with its existing owner. The pure Rust WASI provider passes
its four counter cases on Linux aarch64 at `dev-fast`; this is distinct from
Molt runtime or emitted-program acceptance. Native object-fixture cohorts must
declare their actual compiler instead of inheriting it from another check.
Native and WASM final-link tests also require their declared compilers, linkers
and execution hosts locally: the optional tool probes and successful early
returns are removed across both backends. Actual compilation and execution own
failure diagnostics; no per-test version subprocess is needed. Shared fixture
changes select all compiled consumers. Linux aarch64 native and LLVM cohorts
pass at `release-fast`, TIR/WASM and standalone C-API link/tests at `dev-fast`,
and the default-feature runtime semantic gate at `release-output`.
The buffer-eligibility fixture had incorrectly
adopted StoreIndex's borrowed statement receiver as an owned result.
Its caller now discards that ABI return after checking success identity, retaining
the actual failure, mutation and export-retirement oracles. Production statement
ownership remains unchanged; the expanded runtime gate qualifies this repair.
Other CLI C-API and extension cells that skip when a compiler is absent remain
unqualified; their prerequisites and actual executions remain V1-07 obligations.
This work is development-only. Performance probes, other platform/version cells
and the installed release matrix remain unqualified; V1.0 release is still held.

Differential proof declarations now select their host compiler independently
from their guest build profile. The development text/codec cohort previously
requested a development guest while leaving the host compiler at its release
default, causing an unintended release compiler build. All seven proof
declarations now name their host choice; ordinary compiler defaults remain
unchanged. Matching profiles does not merge distinct backend feature graphs.
Their remaining build cost belongs to HF-334.

CPython's `_json.scanstring` accepts an omitted `strict` argument with value
`True`. Its direct intrinsic export omitted that default. The existing manifest
default authority now declares it, preserving one callable and the fixed
three-argument runtime ABI across registry, bootstrap and compiled handles.
The owning differential exercises both `_json` and `json.decoder` aliases,
omitted and explicit strictness, control-character rejection, and positional-only
arity/keyword rejection. The generator regression fails with the old declaration;
all 54 owning Python controls and the actual native/WASM consumer cohort pass.
Other target versions, platforms and release acceptance remain unqualified.

Backend cache fixtures must own their request environment. Pure cache-key,
single-flight and byte-storage tests now enter the existing typed empty scope;
object-publication fixtures construct explicit codegen settings. Tests with
deliberate semantic settings retain their nonempty scopes, and process-admission
controls still reject invalid settings. Their baseline uses the canonical
request-key set instead of a duplicated four-key subset. An isolated self-image
replay poisons native-partition and common codegen settings before running the
complete owning cache modules. Sixteen old tests fail with an invalid
native-partition setting; poisoning the common codegen setting as well exposes
24 failures. The corrected native library/binary gate and the compiler-authorities
daemon feature graph pass on Linux aarch64, including the isolated replay.
Other platform cells remain unverified.
These are development-only fixture changes, with no emitted-program lock or
environment lookup.

Linux process snapshots can legitimately report a zero boot-relative birth
value. Development custody now retains those observations while preserving
ambiguous live identities from automatic retirement; marker generations still
require positive birth identities. Both the Linux and macOS 125-case custody
cohorts pass, including the original native sweep failure and receipt refusal
controls. This repairs that admission boundary; V1-12's remaining process,
platform and signaling obligations stay open. No new guest work is introduced.

MIME Base64 decoding and binascii now share the same native ASCII-buffer
converter, parser and result owner. MIME decoding retains the input lease
instead of copying its entire input, and applies Clinic's exporter-error policy
after its public format check. The existing differential carrier covers all
exporter exception classes and enclosing-handler context. These are emitted
runtime changes. The 838-line consumer oracle passes actual native and WASM
execution for Python 3.12; regex consumers, runtime fault controls and the other
admitted Python-version cells remain under qualification.

Builtin sequence descriptors now use the existing declaration and subscription
authorities, including exact arbitrary-precision range slicing through the same
normalizer as `slice.indices`. Integer indexing retains its fast path; range
slicing does no work proportional to the number of elements. The descriptor
and large-range consumer programs pass native and WASM execution against
Python 3.12; allocation-failure controls and other guest-version cells remain
under qualification.

Capture extraction now shares one physical text/bytes slice authority and the
existing aggregate owner. It preserves root errors and lossless WTF-8, clamps
saved spans to the current mutable buffer, and retires partial captures on every
failure. The copied whole-text/`Vec<char>` lane and its separate tuple builder
are removed. Actual native and WASM consumers now preserve the four previously
overwritten diagnostics and mutable-buffer clamping. The expanded consumer
exposed a scalar-only replacement conversion and unordered named-group
publication; their source migration now uses the shared lossless text codec and
one insertion-ordered name catalog, with closed replacement-error variants.
The codec's former runtime-local facades and direct dependency are removed,
and its primitive tests join the existing regex proof cohort. The expanded
bytes-admission, parity and Unicode-flags programs now pass actual native and
WASM execution against CPython 3.12.13; the pure Rust regex/codec cohort passes
150 controls. Native rollback controls and other guest-version cells remain
under HF-322. Shared UTF-8 indexing still scans for ASCII before cache lookup;
that residual classification cost remains a V1-07 obligation. Normal regex
buffer execution exits cleanly, but does not independently qualify the earlier
exceptional-shutdown observation.

Mac runtime allocation-failure, compiled split-runtime and integration
qualification remains held at development storage admission. Its allocation
gate refused before Cargo compilation and supplies no runtime pass or failure.
The existing Linux VM admits storage, but tool capture exposed queue overrides
arriving after DX had already selected cache wrappers and derived output roots.
One requested environment now feeds validation, admission and DX resolution;
the existing child-delivery and queue-owned custody rules remain intact. Its
regression fails on the old ordering and the owning 22 controls pass on both
macOS and Linux. Linux replay then refused an unreadable unrelated system
subtree before Cargo: finite Python/native files had become recursive parent
roots, and Linux also recursively enumerated finite watches. The source now
projects startup roles once, keeps exact/absent/alias inputs finite, and traverses
only their selected ancestors; native resource/archive and environment import
archive consumers move with it. Required input watch failures remain fatal.
The selected macOS Python/toolchain ownership checks pass, including finite
watch arming, negative selectors, aliases and required-root refusal. The Linux
prechecks also pass after binding the basename-interpreter fixture's PATH to
its selected installation, as CPython's startup algorithm requires. The
allocation-observer request now passes input-watch capture and reaches Cargo.
Its first compilation exposed four stale regex ownership-test calls to a removed
root snapshot API. Those consumers now use the existing scoped borrowed read,
which preserves their independent reference-count oracle without adding pins;
both aggregate-ownership cases join the existing observer policy. The optimized
Linux build then succeeds: twelve controls pass, including capture rollback and
the public ABI allocation controls. The remaining ordinary-aggregate test used
identifier-only fragments and observed immortal intern-pool entries, rather
than newly allocated children. Its data now selects ordinary computed strings
while retaining the exact ownership assertions. At `c45880998`, the optimized
Linux/aarch64 observer build and all thirteen fresh-process controls pass
(eleven runtime, two public ABI), reusing the existing Cargo workspace. This
qualifies the selected ownership and allocation-refusal boundaries, not timed
performance, the complete ordinary runtime suite, or unexecuted platforms.
Computed identifier retention remains open under V1-20. The environment locator
still arms base installation prefixes to cover startup selectors not represented in its
location schema; that broader development cost remains under V1-07 and must be
reconciled with the existing startup-selection authority. These changes
add nothing to emitted programs. The bounded target results above do not
qualify unexecuted consumers or authorize release acceptance.

The canonical LLVM setup also exposed two rejected SDK binding selectors before
the compiled WASM consumers could launch. The existing LLVM naming authority
now owns their closed grammar; queue admission, compile identity, supervisor
generation, Cargo workspace and tool-probe reuse share it. Exact SDK selectors
are bound too, and Cargo configuration cannot silently substitute an uncaptured
default or forced value. All 95 focused controls pass on macOS and Linux,
including actual Git probe reuse and filesystem-backed workspace partitioning. Prior-source
controls reproduce unchanged identities after five SDK selector changes; the
corrected identities distinguish them. Compiled consumer qualification remains
required. This adds no cost to emitted programs.

The incoming shared toolchain admission also requires an explicit repository
root through proof execution, integration and generators. Every caller now
forwards its existing plan/checkout/source authority, and omitted roots fail at
the API boundary. The 16 affected admission controls have relevant passing
macOS evidence, including real generator fingerprints and a real integration
gate; two additional executor/provider controls pass. This is bounded consumer
qualification, with Linux/Windows and full integration still required.

The first compiled Linux/aarch64 host-boundaries cohort at `c5451e1af` fails
all nine parametrized cases before semantic qualification. Split builds reject
a stale browser-asset projection of the generated WASM ABI; linked builds hit
an optimizer process cap near 0.69 GiB at about 0.8 GiB RSS. Nested guards have
reinterpreted an inherited allocation as a new machine and repeatedly applied
the host reserve and allocation fractions. The existing generator DAG and host
capacity authorities own these corrections; the warmed Cargo workspace is
retained. A separate queue pytest warning also exposes a disabled cache plugin
beside active cache configuration. No consumer pass or performance acceptance
is inferred from this failed cohort.

The owning corrections now preserve raw host facts and delegated allocations
in one typed snapshot, stop exporting an admitted process cap as raw available
memory, and intersect the backend budget with that cap after the raw reserve.
Independent same/rotating-prefix nesting and pressure regressions pass; the
unknown-host fallback, scheduling consumers and explicit raw override transport
have focused controls. Targeted generator writes now traverse the existing
downstream dependency graph, and ABI generation repairs its browser consumer
together. Split builds also validate that existing closure before discovery or
Cargo work, retaining late publication mutation checks; the added names-only
admission measured 2.41 ms in one local sample. Queue pytest keeps its cache
plugin and writes into admitted scratch.
These are development/compiler changes with no emitted-runtime work. The
compiled consumer qualification below now passes; canonical integration and its
owning Rust budget/cache controls remain required.

A subsequent held-source Linux/aarch64 run executes all nine WASM cases
successfully in 395.25 seconds, with native process closure complete and a
2.78 GiB peak process tree. The queue nevertheless rejects its input custody:
a concurrent development-side integration dry-run without Python `-B` wrote
five imported bytecode caches into the watched source. This is an operator
launch violation, not evidence of a compiler-child policy gap. The original
failed receipt remains rejected; read-only launch capsules and the owning
runbook now require no-write Python startup while a source tree is held.
Admissible compiled replay is still required. Family inspection additionally
found two read-only isolated launchers (installed `ty` validation and the
verified-subset CPython identity probe) that lacked explicit `-B`. Both now
carry it; real disposable-site startup controls fail without the flag despite
inherited cache settings. These adjacent omissions did not cause the rejected
WASM run. Their repair is compiler/development-only.

The reconciled source now passes admissible Linux/aarch64 Python 3.12 compiled
qualification: nine host-boundary, final-TIR and finder cases, the separate GPU
retained-bytes regression, and the Falcon package-entry regression. All three
runs have complete native process closure, no custody violations and accepted
source stability. Their largest observed process tree is 4.14 GiB. The latter
two runs reuse the first run's admitted Cargo generation; target selection takes
0.60 and 0.55 seconds. These are scoped correctness/resource observations,
not comparative performance acceptance. Falcon uses the existing stub-model
fixture to prove driver/package integration; it does not qualify real inference.
Other OS/architecture, browser execution and Python-version acceptance remain
with the public matrix and V1-35. Canonical publication remains required.

Integration now binds attribution, changed-clippy and changed-rustfmt gates
to its captured full upstream commit. Raw declarations still own prerequisite
identity, while the executed copies use that one immutable base. Controls with
separate source-sync/publication remotes and a moved tracking ref reject the
old `origin/main` ambiguity; default and non-default remote cases pass locally.
This corrects development qualification and adds no emitted-runtime work.

The incoming pytest worker policy is reconciled with the typed capacity owner:
worker sizing and executor shares consume one memory snapshot, and an inherited
slice does not incur another host reserve. Executor sharing uses the selected
resource classes' existing concurrency limits, so a serialized Cargo cohort is
not divided by idle worker slots. This is a static concurrency upper bound;
elastic peer allocation and the host-wide jobserver remain HF-334 obligations.
Merged and selector-bearing landing cohorts also retain the largest memory
envelope from their existing owning commands. A derived prefix index preserves
file, directory and node boundaries without test collection or filesystem
scans; uncovered targets keep the one shared ad hoc default. This closes the
new underallocation path where larger-unit suites silently inherited 2.5 GiB.
No emitted-program work is added.

CI change selection now derives each family's literal test-target ownership
from its validated command arguments once when loading the existing proof plan.
Selection and generated projections consume the same resolved inputs; the
duplicate exact test entries are removed from the manifest. This repairs 25
omitted file edges without another registry, test collection or filesystem
scan. Additional dependency globs remain explicit. Directory arguments are
conservative ownership boundaries: a command that also declares a narrower
filter can select its family for an unrelated descendant change. More precise
semantic dependency selection and scheduler consolidation remain under HF-334.
This is development-side work only.

Local landing policy merges plain pytest targets into one parallel invocation;
selector-bearing gates retain their declared scope. The driver and policy share
one test-path/node-ID validator, including root containment. Generated batches
retain argument vectors through process custody on every platform; shell text
is only their diagnostic/projection form. Upstream placeholder validation applies
to authored shell gates, preserving literal braces and delimiters in pytest
parameter IDs. First-occurrence deduplication uses
expected linear work, and failed as well as successful gates contribute to the
existing timing summary. These are development costs, with no emitted-program
work. Targeted selection and actual selected-interpreter/failure controls pass
on macOS arm64; Windows argument dispatch has modeled boundary controls and
still requires native qualification under V1-07. Local Clippy selection reuses
an equivalent declared host cell, preserving its identity and budget instead of
applying the Linux deadline on macOS. All execution fields must agree; only
scheduling coordinates may differ. Existing unmatched feature commands retain
their declared contract.

The V1-01 compiler input migration now has one complete-frame contract: a
closed format selector, same-reader binary EOF checks, shared NDJSON envelope
states, and one JSON decoder for one-shot and daemon leases. Cache-only requests
keep their unused leases unopened. The implementation adds no input hash, extra
read pass or emitted-program checks. Its owning binary and codec proofs passed on macOS arm64 with CBOR enabled
and disabled (HF-309). Consumed-byte origin/cache derivation and
authenticated release admission remain open under V1-01.

The daemon now owns complete typed target and actual semantic-environment
identity across cache lookup, publication and single-flight coordination
(HF-311/HF-315). Native and WASM producers exercise both cache tiers,
changed-target/environment misses and unchanged-artifact replay on macOS arm64.
Daemon and TIR residency share one weighted owner: keys, request context,
quarantine paths and output allocations participate in admission, and warm hits
promote a live node without stale generations or allocation. The
[daemon design](../design/backend_compile_daemon.md#resident-ownership-and-eviction)
owns transitions, costs and the distinction between charged ownership and
process RSS. Caller IR keys still require consumed-input binding under V1-01;
full resource/performance and other-platform qualification remain V1-07
obligations. Emitted binaries gain no checks.

The current V1-01 input integration reuses the preserved Cargo per-unit reader
and native generation publisher. Publication now requires coverage for files,
declared directory roots and package-wide watches. Directory names participate
in the existing source-tree digest, including empty-directory additions and
removals. Cargo's strict environment decoding, Windows OUT_DIR and UNC paths,
ambiguous evidence refusal and whitespace-trimmed build-script directives share
the same reader; that reader belongs to the runtime tooling identity. The
[Cargo input design](../design/cargo_input_authority.md) records the transition
and costs. Runtime-family input records, environment completeness, cross-platform
qualification and authenticated compiler/runtime used-byte admission remain
open. These are compiler/development checks, with no emitted-program work.
On macOS arm64, a current native `dev` build with `dev-fast` compiler/runtime,
edge stdlib and target Python 3.12 passed actual Cargo coverage and atomic
generation publication. Its `bench_sum` executable matches CPython 3.12.15 in
stdout/stderr/exit with empty executable and Python import paths, and both
guarded processes close their descendants. This qualifies that publication and
execution cell only; other platforms, profiles and WASM publication stay open.

The V1-01/V1-07 measurement integration executes WASM benchmarks through
the declared deployment manifest and the public runner, and consumes typed
guard timing/RSS/closure facts directly. It removes two Python wrapper launches
per sample and guest-stderr metadata parsing. Child time excludes guard cleanup;
WASM host diagnostics remain retained separately from exact guest bytes.
Independent review exposed capture substitution, split-context recycled-FD
shutdown writes, CLI cwd drift and failed trace admission; family regressions
cover their corrected boundaries. This is development-side measurement work;
emitted guest binaries gain no instrumentation. The public scoreboard still
refuses the missing WASM startup budget, and a busy host cannot establish
performance acceptance. Every failed cold, warmup or warm attempt now refuses
measurement acceptance across both runtimes and all repeats; a failed reference
run cannot become a compatibility exclusion. Full authenticated release admission
remains open. Schema 5 carries the admitted Node engine's version/content from
one plan per WASM invocation through each cell, checkpoint, projection, merge
and history receiver. Changed engine bytes or version split comparability;
relocating identical bytes does not. Native boards perform no Node admission.
Legacy records retain their original schema and require remeasurement. This is
host observation, not loaded-byte attestation; missing budgets, full target
qualification and positive release producer admission remain V1-07 obligations.

The bounded linked-WASM `bench_sum` development-profile execution passes all
16 observations against CPython 3.12.13 with exact stdout/stderr/exit parity,
complete descendant closure and retired temporary outputs. Eight Node warning
streams are retained separately. On the busy host, advisory warm process
medians are 1.028117 s for WASM and 0.208687 s for CPython; the linked module
is 27,754.4 KiB. These include engine startup/compilation and do not qualify
release performance, engine-only cost or a before/after improvement. The later
all-attempt admission amendments are separately exercised by the final consumer
proof; the earlier actual execution record retains its original source identity.
Startup/compile cost, runtime reachability and the full profile/platform matrix
remain open V1-07 work.


The qualified boundaries below identify their source versions and limits. The
parent integrator continues to own preserved WIP reconciliation. Coordination records own active
write scopes and private receipts; this ledger owns release status.
`tools/finding_status.py` counts its open and fixed rows and reports identity
defects; no prose here repeats that count. Rows are obligations, not a
completion percentage. Published integration `41bd5b020` reconciles the
captured SSL, source-input/custody, JSON, compiler and runtime donors with
current main. Original donor commits, index and physical bytes remain
preserved. Source integration is distinct from consumer qualification and
publication: changed bare C-ABI and managed-WASM consumers must exercise their
actual contracts before landing. Private coordination records identify exact
source versions, restore locations, qualification and ownership; do not replay
stale donor files over the current authority.

The integrated native runtime, compiler graph and managed-WASM lifecycle gates
pass at `121d94a98`; the final frontend-only correction preserves those Rust
inputs. Standalone C-ABI consumers pass at `b8baad5f4` with the same ABI owner
inputs. Frontend source backends retain an unknown runtime OS, and exception
availability requires positive target facts. These are bounded implementation
qualifications, not acceptance of the complete target/version/profile or
performance matrix. The open requirements below continue to hold v1.0.

Land complete semantic families once their actual consumers pass. An unrelated
open finding does not hold an independently complete repair; an incomplete
consumer migration does. Reuse unchanged qualified evidence, fix the exposed
shared cause, and replay affected cases before broadening verification.
Every repair must retire its replaced implementation and move all consumers
together. A source review, unit pass or generator check does not establish
target execution.

The 24 text-predicate calls now share the existing generated boxed ABI across
native, LLVM and WASM; the 1,645-line native handler is retired. The actual
family table and generated mapper own routing coverage, including rejection of
unreachable audit arms. The executable fixture and its frontend control require
all 24 specialized producers before callback invalidation. On 2026-10-17 that
48-call fixture matches CPython 3.12.15 through Cranelift, LLVM and linked WASM
on the Apple arm64 host, with an empty executable search path and empty Python
home/import paths during target execution. The retained native compilers emit

### Development scheduling and integration cost evidence

Retained HF-334 evidence and obligations; the open row above owns status and
execution order. These historical observations do not establish current acceptance.

**Observed mechanism.** Concurrency is fixed constants and two schedulers: the proof executor runs `executor_max_workers = 4`, landings run pytest at `local_pytest_workers = 4` in a sequential gate loop (one landing summed 404 s of clippy, 411 s of runtime tests and 190 s of pytest), plan commands pin `-n 2` 14 times and pass `-n auto` 10 times (one worker per CPU, no memory bound), `resource_pressure` caps Cargo at 4 jobs of a declared 12 GB (2.35 GB measured), and nested parallelism (xdist workers whose tests start parallel builds) is uncoordinated.

**Recorded evidence.** docs/design/host_capacity.md and an independent audit of every capacity decision, 2026-10-17; HF-335 landed its first slice. Worker count does not bound the landing suites (67/65/62 s at -n 4/8/12): their slowest tests do. 2026-10-17: the guard capped a guarded tree's RSS (33 GB on this Mac) while everything inside sized against the machine (66 GB live); it now exports the cap as `MOLT_HOST_MEMORY_SLICE_BYTES`, which `host_capacity` honors, and the memory reserve rule lives in `host_capacity.reserve_bytes`. 2026-10-17: CI main failed 40 consecutive completed runs (last green 2026-10-14, b5487aef3). A static import-graph selector with Pants-style asset inference caught every break that runs on this host, but 58 of the last 150 main commits reached all 990 test files, because `tests/conftest.py` alone reaches 458 modules. 2026-10-17: receipts carry `worker_peaks`, the largest xdist worker subtree and the top per-test peaks, measured by the guard from the workers' current-test records; on repository.agent-coordination (18 workers) one worker peaked at 219 MB against a 2.0 GB tree. A nested pytest inherited PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER and published as a worker; the writer now takes worker identity from xdist's `config.workerinput`. 2026-10-18: worker units measured per command (macOS arm64) run from 0.22 GiB (repository.agent-coordination) to 4.94 GiB (import-collection); every xdist command declares `--molt-worker-memory-gb` (peak times 1.25), `molt.pytest_capacity_plugin` resolves `-n auto`, the proof executor gives each concurrent command its share of the memory beyond the reserve, and `local_pytest_workers` and CI's `PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS` are deleted; `python.unit.frontend-lowering.macos` went from 162 s at -n 2 to 38 s at 18 workers. Unverified: CI budgets of the suites that run one worker on the 7 GB macOS runner. Linux joined-suite qualification also exposed small-cap protocol tests inheriting a loaded runner’s pre-exec RSS high-water mark: `wait4` reported about 788 MiB after the actual children exited with their expected 0/7 statuses. The finite metadata/protocol control family now uses one fresh guarded pytest observer, preserving all original limits, fixtures and assertions. Lifetime `process_rusage` enforcement and the independent short-lived allocator control remain intact. The [capacity contract](../design/host_capacity.md#executable-image-and-lifetime-memory) distinguishes lifetime, sampled-tree and executable-image measurements; correct benchmark attribution remains required, not waived.

**Remaining qualification.** Per the design: declared per-unit needs sized from measured receipt peaks; `-n auto` resolved by the `pytest_xdist_auto_num_workers` hook; landing gates through the proof executor, longest first; one GNU make jobserver for CPU and per-peer memory slices; operation-owned shared source records with volume placement justified by measurement; the same authority on each farm machine. Closes HF-27, HF-68, HF-170 and HF-225 with it. Landing selection is hand-maintained globs: three contract tests broke main on 2026-10-17 because no rule ran them (HF-331, HF-332, HF-336), and a fourth: 3d2b54010 gave uv a process-image probe in `tools/proof_plan.toml`, and no landing ran `tests/tools/test_custody_apparatus.py`, whose hand-built uv identity had no inventory (fixed by deleting that duplicate: the producer-backed uv test in `tests/tools/test_proof_queue.py` proves the same receiver and fails when its digest check is removed); derive each landing's tests from proof-plan test ownership and the plan's family inputs, one selection authority instead of two. The landing design is docs/design/landing_queue.md: main advances only to a commit that passed its family-selected pre-push commands on every cell, through one queue with rollups and bisection on the owner's machines, with a receipt per candidate and no second path to main. A clean macOS landing exposed a fresh-observer helper that cleared project addopts and thereby removed the explicit guard configuration plugin: the selected body passed, but pytest wrote cache into source custody. The helper now explicitly loads that canonical plugin and runs serially without an xdist option. Real fresh-project controls cover plugin autoload on and off, exact-node execution and external cache placement. Owning local selection now includes checkout-output and fresh-observer regression families; CI ownership was already present. The combined macOS custody/helper consumer cohort passes 344 controls with four platform skips; Ruff, generated projection synchronization and all eight changed-path owner selections pass. Linux inherited-image qualification remains a separate platform cell. Local unfiltered pytest retains one collection and its existing maximum owning worker envelope; literal selections remain independent. A serial resource-group experiment was retired before landing because it repeated startup and serialized stragglers without an established whole-campaign benefit. Native pytest duration reporting exposes bounded stragglers on required runs. Concurrency belongs to the existing proof executor and shared capacity authority, not another scheduler or result cache. Late command initialization also exposed unconditional repository import rebinding after a caller had captured its admitted path. The shared binder now preserves an admitted canonical root/src prefix while retaining full loaded-package custody validation; unsafe aliases and missing roots repair in one publication. The unchanged selected-catalog oracle and a fresh precollection lifecycle regression pass with the owning binder controls (79 checks). These are development-side repairs; full family scheduling and platform qualification remain open. Broadened tooling type checks also expose 28 existing proof-plan executor/receipt diagnostics (the same baseline and candidate messages); these type-contract defects remain mandatory family work, not green typing or a release waiver. A Fleet global reaper was independently proven to cause three macOS landing SIGTERM interruptions: it matched `/.codex/worktrees/` in ordinary Python command lines and treated `/dev/null` stdin as abandonment despite live parents. Its exact PID/timestamp log matches all three runs, and a read-only live-parent control reproduces the false positive. The approved Mac repair persistently disables and unloads that job and removes its installed startup definition. Existing Linux/Windows installations have not been removed, and BEAM execution remains unverified because its dependencies are unavailable. This fixes the proven host interruption mechanism without adding work to emitted programs; it does not close the remaining scheduler, type-contract or release obligations. That job is disabled pending an explicit request to run it; local Fleet source migrates all five launchers, both Windows repository markers and exact module/port duplicate detection to the installed proxy owner. Seven owning controls pass, including a fresh isolated child that loads the actual installed public entrypoint without opening a listener. The two Fleet repairs are committed locally, not deployed to other machines or published.

Cache retention is also an open development-side ownership migration. The
current generic pruner can select live native compilation scratch and lock files,
and treats the complete frontend lowering cache as one eviction unit. Its
preserved native entry/lock migration must be reconciled through all current
producers, readers and cleanup consumers before automatic broad eviction is
enabled. Immutable frontend leaves can be evicted independently because readers
first hydrate private copies and treat missing shared entries as cache misses.
Native daemon scratch requires its actual execution owner; a requesting guard
may finish before that daemon does. Automatic retention must use one bounded,
shared policy without scans on object publication or emitted-program work.
V1-25 owns this incomplete migration and its concurrency, cleanup and cost proofs.

The resulting family review exposes a broader ownership-policy defect: ordinary
semantic temporaries use error-suppressing release guards. This includes C
callback results, retained call arguments, descriptors, iterators, parsing
cleanup, runtime-core value owners and the HTTP release bridge. A retained
container reference can become the last owner when a callback removes the
original edge. Default drop, early return and unwind must therefore implement
the same declared retirement policy. CPython source is the oracle for each
operation's error visibility and release order; cleanup naming alone does not
justify suppression.

The assembled correction uses static ownership policies with ordinary semantic
release, explicitly protected suppression/projection and completed native-to-runtime
error custody. Policies add no payload, dynamic dispatch or emitted validation.
The migration must classify every affected producer and consumer, delete the
ambiguous replaced release authority, and retain explicit finalizer, unraisable,
rollback and handled-exception contracts where their semantics require protection.
Raised-state replacement must publish the selected next error before retiring
the old value. Normalization preserves CPython's distinct constructor and input
retirement phases. Its typed field producers must distinguish actual operation
failure from an already pending error; a status-correct consumer cannot compensate
for a producer that rejects all pending state. Independent native controls must
exercise both incoming C and runtime errors, sole ownership, callback reentry,
exact pending-error identity and traceback, release ordering, early exits and
unchanged output on failure. No source census or green isolated helper qualifies
this migration. Complete standalone/runtime consumers, applicable satellite and
target cells, and performance measurements remain required before landing.
